title: Simplifying Algebraic Fractions
subject: Mathematics
subtopic: Factorise and cancel, multiply, divide, add and subtract

scenes.heading: Simplifying Algebraic Fractions
scenes.subheading: Grade 9 Mathematics · Factorisation and equations, part 2
scenes.narration: Welcome to part two of our Grade 9 series on factorisation and equations. In this lesson we use factorising to simplify algebraic fractions, and we add and subtract them.

scenes.heading: The rules
bullets: Factorise the top and the bottom first
Then cancel common factors, never single terms
To add or subtract, write every fraction over the LCD
scenes.narration: Three rules. First, factorise the top and the bottom. Then cancel common factors, but never single terms. And to add or subtract fractions, write every fraction over the lowest common denominator.

scenes.heading: Example 1
scenes.narration: Simplify x squared minus nine, over x plus three. The top is a difference of two squares: x minus three, times x plus three. Now x plus three is a factor on top and at the bottom, so it cancels. The answer is x minus three.

scenes.heading: Example 2
scenes.narration: Simplify x squared plus five x plus six, over x squared minus four. Factorise the top: x plus two, times x plus three. Factorise the bottom: x minus two, times x plus two. Cancel the common factor x plus two. The answer is x plus three, over x minus two.

scenes.heading: Example 3: Dividing
scenes.narration: Simplify two x plus six over x squared, divided by x plus three over x. To divide, multiply by the reciprocal of the second fraction. Factorise two x plus six as two times, x plus three. Now cancel x plus three, and cancel one x from x squared. The answer is two over x.

scenes.heading: Example 4: Adding
scenes.narration: Simplify x over three plus x over four. The LCD is twelve. x over three is four x over twelve, and x over four is three x over twelve. Add the tops: seven x over twelve.

scenes.heading: Example 5: Subtracting
scenes.narration: Simplify two x plus one over three, minus x minus one over two. The LCD is six. Multiply the first top by two and the second top by three, and keep the tops in brackets. Expand: four x plus two, minus three x, plus three. Watch the sign: negative three times negative one is plus three. Simplify: x plus five, over six.

scenes.heading: Example 6: x in the denominator
scenes.narration: Simplify three over x, plus two over x squared. The LCD is x squared. Multiply the top and bottom of the first fraction by x, to get three x over x squared. Now add: three x plus two, over x squared.
